label: Mercado Libre
terms_note: Free developer app at developers.mercadolibre.com; only the seller's ADMIN account can authorise the app (operators cannot); tokens die on password / secret change or 4+ months inactivity; refresh token single-use; redirect URI must match exactly; test users for development; rate limits per app (403 / 429 — numbers not on the pages read); listing fees + sales commission per site and listing_type.

discovery.auth: oauth2 (app id + secret; authorization-code with PKCE; access 6 h, single-use refresh token 6 months; scopes offline_access read write)
sdks: official SDKs per language linked from the developer portal

rate_limits: 1,500 requests/min per seller (429) — from search; auth page opened but JS-rendered

auth: 1. Create the app on the developer portal → app id + secret key; register the exact redirect URI; enable notification topics.
2. Seller (admin account) authorises: authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256) → code → POST /oauth/token → access_token (6 h) + refresh_token (single-use, 6 months).
3. Refresh proactively; store the newest refresh token only (old ones are invalid).

endpoints.notes: title, category_id (predict via /sites/{site}/domain_discovery/search), price, currency_id, available_quantity, buying_mode buy_it_now, listing_type_id, attributes (ITEM_CONDITION, BRAND, GTIN…), pictures ≤ 6, sale_terms, shipping

endpoints.purpose: update price, available_quantity, status (paused / closed), pictures
endpoints.notes: sold/available quantities visible only with the owner token

endpoints.call: GET /shipments/{id} · Mercado Envíos labels · custom tracking update

endpoints.purpose: topics orders_v2, shipments, items, questions, claims, messages

reference.limits: Per-app limits with 429 / 403 responses; numbers not published on the pages read. - Developer terms of the portal; seller authorises via OAuth (admin only). - Listing type sets fees + exposure; immediate-payment rules vary by site / category. - Refresh token is single-use — persist the newest one (our `_persist_refresh` path).
mcp_sdk: SDK: official SDKs per language linked from the developer portal

sandbox.notes: Mercado Libre has no sandbox: 'We do not have a test environment or sandbox to run tests: we make it possible to use test users for verification directly in production.' Create up to 10 test users with POST https://api.mercadolibre.com/users/test_user {site_id} using a production access token, save their credentials at once (they cannot be listed later), and authorize the app as a test seller; test users only transact with other test users' listings and expire after a while.

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: App ID of your application (developers.mercadolibre.com > My applications); sent as client_id in the token request body.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: Secret Key of the same application; sent as client_secret in the token request body.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Refresh token (TG-...) from a one-time authorization-code consent by the seller's ADMIN account (valid 6 months). It is SINGLE-USE: every refresh returns a new access token (6 h) and a new refresh token, and only the last one issued is accepted. The runtime keeps a rotated refresh token in memory; set PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR to also save it (<dir>/<platform>.json, mode 0600) so it is preferred over this variable on the next start. Without the state directory, a restart after the first refresh needs a fresh refresh token.

config_fields.name: seller_id
config_fields.help: Numeric Mercado Libre user id of the seller (the `id` returned by GET /users/me); used as the seller filter of the order search.

me.note: GET /users/me returns the authorised user {id, nickname, site_id, country_id, ...}; its id is the seller_id config value.

update_listing.note: PUT /items/{item_id} {title, price, available_quantity} with only the given fields (Sync and modify listings). The title can only change while sold_quantity = 0; `description` has its own endpoint (/items/{id}/description) and is not mapped. The listing guide points to the Prices API for price management. Returns the item; `status` is active|paused|closed|under_review...

end_listing.note: PUT /items/{item_id} {status: paused} takes the listing off sale and out of view, reversible with status active. `closed` (final, can only be relisted) and the deleted flag are not used.

set_inventory.note: PUT /items/{item_id} {available_quantity} sets stock; 0 auto-pauses the item (out_of_stock) on MLB, MLA, MLM, MLC, MPE and MLV, and a positive value reactivates it. `listing_id` (item id, e.g. MLA1136716168) is required; items are not addressed by SKU. Variation stock is per variation (not mapped).

list_orders.note: GET /orders/search?seller={seller_id}&order.status(confirmed|payment_required|payment_in_process|partially_paid|paid|cancelled...; comma-separated)&order.date_created.from(ISO-8601, hour precision)&sort=date_desc&offset&limit (the documented page size is 50). Returns {results[{id, status, total_amount, currency_id, date_created, shipping{id}}], paging{total, offset, limit}}.

not_offered.create_listing: POST /items requires category_id (predicted per product), listing_type_id, currency_id, condition, buying_mode, pictures and the category's required attributes (BRAND, MODEL, GTIN, ...) — none of which the vocabulary carries; the category attributes differ per category.
not_offered.mark_shipped: Marking an ME1 (seller-shipped) order as dispatched is POST /shipments/{shipment_id}/seller_notifications {payload{service_id (per site), comment, date}, tracking_number, tracking_url, status: shipped, substatus: null}; the shipment id comes from GET /orders/{order_id}/shipments first (two calls). Mercado Envíos ME2 shipments are tracked by the carrier.
not_offered.listing_metrics: No per-item visits endpoint confirmed this pass (the visits documentation page did not load); not mapped.
